title: One in eleven US AI job ads now asks for MCP
description: The tools US employers ask for in AI job ads: PyTorch leads, MCP is in 1 in 11 ads, and prompt engineering is a skill, never a job title.
dek: MCP, the standard way AI agents connect to software, appears in 193 of 2,046 recent US AI job ads. Prompt engineering appears in 258, but never as a job title.
findings: PyTorch, the most used framework for building models, is the most requested tool, in 427 ads.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets an AI agent use other software. It appears in 193 ads from 159 employers, about 1 in 11 ads.
Prompt engineering is asked for in 258 ads, but none of the 2,046 ads is titled prompt engineer. It became a skill, not a job.
Among data platforms, Databricks (200 ads) leads Snowflake (132). Among cloud AI services, Azure OpenAI (113) leads AWS Bedrock (88) and Google Vertex AI (82).

chart.title: US AI job ads naming each tool or skill
chart.subtitle: Ads posted between 21 and 25 Nov 2026; 2,046 ads after reposts removed

method: I pulled the 3,000 newest US job ads with AI or machine-learning job titles posted between 21 and 25 Nov 2026, from the jobspipe job index, and removed reposts, leaving 2,046.
A tool counts when the ad's description names it as a whole word or phrase.
'MCP' as in 'Microsoft Certified Professional' is excluded; a hand check found about 1 in 12 raw matches meant that.
No job title in the sample contains 'prompt engineer'.
